Over the last couple of months, though, it has become incredibly intense and constant, and I haven't had any breaks from these thoughts at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there have been any periods, even brief ones, where you questioned the reality of these beliefs about people working against you, or have they always felt completely true to you since they started?\n\nPatient: Honestly, they have always felt completely real to me, and I haven't had any moments where I truly doubted it. Even when my sister or colleagues tell me I'm just overthinking things, I can't shake the feeling at all. To me, it just feels like an absolute fact that they are working together against me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as depression or mania, alongside these persistent thoughts of being targeted, or have your emotions remained relatively stable despite these beliefs?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I experience extreme highs like mania, and it's not really typical sadness or depression either. Instead, I just feel completely flat, empty, and disconnected from everything around me. Most days I just sit in my apartment with the TV on mute, ignoring everyone and feeling like I'm just going through the motions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, especially in relation to these beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't actually there. For me, it has really just been this constant, overwhelming feeling that these specific people are actively working together to ruin me. That is the only thing I've been experiencing, but it feels completely real.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where these thoughts of people working against you went away completely for at least a month, or have they been continuous since they started?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't gone away at all. The general feeling that people were against me started slowly two years ago and has gradually worsened, but over the last couple of months, the intense belief that they are actively coordinating to ruin me has been completely continuous without any breaks.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're in danger or that your life is being threatened by these people you believe are working against you?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've felt like my life was in direct physical danger, but I definitely haven't felt safe or welcome in certain spaces, which is why I've cut trips short and isolated myself. The constant anxiety and stress of feeling like they are coordinating to ruin me has just made it feel easier to stay hidden away. It's incredibly exhausting to carry that fear, even if it isn't a physical threat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning, aside from what you've already mentioned, that you attribute to these beliefs or to any other reason?\n\nPatient: Yes, my professional practice has taken a massive hit—I've had to cut my hours way back and have lost several long-term clients because I just can't manage it anymore. It definitely doesn't feel like some random, larger plot; it is a targeted effort to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how you think these people's alleged actions against you are organized, and if you believe there is a leader or a specific method they use to coordinate their efforts?\n\nPatient: I believe they use a quiet group chat or email chain to coordinate, which feels especially obvious whenever a client reschedules or a patron doesn't reply to me. I'm not sure if there is one specific leader behind it all, but I am convinced this group communication is how they organize their efforts to freeze me out and ruin my name.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that you believe a specific group of people is working against you, but can you tell me if you think this belief is based on any actual events or evidence that you've observed, or if it's more of a general feeling that you have?\n\nPatient: It started as a strong gut feeling, but now I see what I believe is clear evidence, like clients suddenly rescheduling meetings or art patrons not returning my emails. I feel these are coordinated actions, like a quiet group chat or email chain meant to freeze me out. Even though others tell me I'm just overthinking these minor setbacks, to me it feels like concrete proof."

It has just felt safer to stay isolated in my apartment.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about people working against you, and have they been persistent or have there been periods where you didn't think about them at all?\n\nPatient: It first started gradually about two years ago after a really difficult breakup, but it was more in the background back then. Over the last couple of months, though, it has become incredibly intense and constant, and I haven't had any breaks from these thoughts at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there have been any periods, even brief ones, where you questioned the reality of these beliefs about people working against you, or have they always felt completely true to you since they started?\n\nPatient: Honestly, they have always felt completely real to me, and I haven't had any moments where I truly doubted it. Even when my sister or colleagues tell me I'm just overthinking things, I can't shake the feeling at all. To me, it just feels like an absolute fact that they are working together against me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as depression or mania, alongside these persistent thoughts of being targeted, or have your emotions remained relatively stable despite these beliefs?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I experience extreme highs like mania, and it's not really typical sadness or depression either. Instead, I just feel completely flat, empty, and disconnected from everything around me. That is the only thing I've been experiencing, but it feels completely real.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where these thoughts of people working against you went away completely for at least a month, or have they been continuous since they started?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't gone away at all. The constant anxiety and stress of feeling like they are coordinating to ruin me has just made it feel easier to stay hidden away. My only concern is this specific group of people in my professional and art circles who are working to ruin my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being controlled or influenced by these people you believe are working against you, or is it solely the belief that they are trying to damage your reputation?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like they are controlling my thoughts, feelings, or physical actions at all. It is solely the belief that they are coordinating behind my back to freeze me out of my practice and social circle. I am just convinced that there is an external plot to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you believe these people's actions against you are specifically aimed at you, or if you think it's part of a larger plot that just happens to involve you?\n\nPatient: I am certain that this is specifically and personally aimed at me. It definitely doesn't feel like some random, larger plot; it is a targeted effort to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how you think these people's alleged actions against you are organized, and if you believe there is a leader or a specific method they use to coordinate their efforts?\n\nPatient: I believe they use a quiet group chat or email chain to coordinate, which feels especially obvious whenever a client reschedules or a patron doesn't reply to me. I'm not sure if there is one specific leader behind it all, but I am convinced this group communication is how they organize their efforts to freeze me out and ruin my name.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that you believe a specific group of people is working against you, but can you tell me if you think this belief is based on any actual events or evidence that you've observed, or if it's more of a general feeling that you have?\n\nPatient: It started as a strong gut feeling, but now I see what I believe is clear evidence, like clients suddenly rescheduling meetings or art patrons not returning my emails. Instead, I just feel completely flat, empty, and disconnected from everything around me. Most days I just sit in my apartment with the TV on mute, ignoring everyone and feeling like I'm just going through the motions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, especially in relation to these beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't actually there. For me, it has really just been this constant, overwhelming feeling that these specific people are actively working together to ruin me. That is the only thing I've been experiencing, but it feels completely real.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where these thoughts of people working against you went away completely for at least a month, or have they been continuous since they started?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't gone away at all. The general feeling that people were against me started slowly two years ago and has gradually worsened, but over the last couple of months, the intense belief that they are actively coordinating to ruin me has been completely continuous without any breaks.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're in danger or that your life is being threatened by these people you believe are working against you?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've felt like my life was in direct physical danger, but I definitely haven't felt safe or welcome in certain spaces, which is why I've cut trips short and isolated myself. The constant anxiety and stress of feeling like they are coordinating to ruin me has just made it feel easier to stay hidden away. It's incredibly exhausting to carry that fear, even if it isn't a physical threat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning, aside from what you've already mentioned, that you attribute to these beliefs or to any other reason?\n\nPatient: Yes, my professional practice has taken a massive hit—I've had to cut my hours way back and have lost several long-term clients because I just can't manage it anymore. Socially, I've become almost completely isolated, barely seeing my friends or family because I constantly cancel plans or avoid any events where I think those people might show up.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant disorganized thinking or speech, or exhibited any catatonic behavior, alongside these persistent beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't experienced any disorganized speech, confused thinking, or unusual physical behaviors like that. My thoughts and speech feel clear to me. My main struggle is really just the constant worry about these people working together to ruin my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other types of delusions, such as delusions of grandeur, being controlled, or having a special mission, beyond the belief that these specific people are working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. I don't feel like I have any special powers, missions, or that anyone else is controlling my actions. My only concern is this specific group of people in my professional and art circles who are working to ruin my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being controlled or influenced by these people you believe are working against you, or is it solely the belief that they are trying to damage your reputation?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like they are controlling my thoughts, feelings, or physical actions at all. It is solely the belief that they are coordinating behind my back to freeze me out of my practice and social circle. I am just convinced that there is an external plot to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you believe these people's actions against you are specifically aimed at you, or if you think it's part of a larger plot that just happens to involve you?\n\nPatient: I am certain that this is specifically and personally aimed at me. I believe this specific group in my professional and art circles is actively coordinating through a private group chat or email chain to freeze me out and ruin my practice. It definitely doesn't feel like some random, larger plot; it is a targeted effort to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how you think these people's alleged actions against you are organized, and if you believe there is a leader or a specific method they use to coordinate their efforts?\n\nPatient: I believe they use a quiet group chat or email chain to coordinate, which feels especially obvious whenever a client reschedules or a patron doesn't reply to me. I'm not sure if there is one specific leader behind it all, but I am convinced this group communication is how they organize their efforts to freeze me out and ruin my name.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that you believe a specific group of people is working against you, but can you tell me if you think this belief is based on any actual events or evidence that you've observed, or if it's more of a general feeling that you have?\n\nPatient: It started as a strong gut feeling, but now I see what I believe is clear evidence, like clients suddenly rescheduling meetings or art patrons not returning my emails. I feel these are coordinated actions, like a quiet group chat or email chain meant to freeze me out. My struggles have really just been centered around the constant stress regarding those people in my professional and art circles.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific actions or events that you believe will happen if these people succeed in their alleged plot against you, and how that affects your daily life and decisions?"

That is the only thing I've been experiencing, but it feels completely real.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where these thoughts of people working against you went away completely for at least a month, or have they been continuous since they started?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't gone away at all. The constant anxiety and stress of feeling like they are coordinating to ruin me has just made it feel easier to stay hidden away. It's incredibly exhausting to carry that fear, even if it isn't a physical threat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning, aside from what you've already mentioned, that you attribute to these beliefs or to any other reason?\n\nPatient: Yes, my professional practice has taken a massive hit—I've had to cut my hours way back and have lost several long-term clients because I just can't manage it anymore. Socially, I've become almost completely isolated, barely seeing my friends or family because I constantly cancel plans or avoid any events where I think those people might show up.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant disorganized thinking or speech, or exhibited any catatonic behavior, alongside these persistent beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't experienced any disorganized speech, confused thinking, or unusual physical behaviors like that. My main struggle is really just the constant worry about these people working together to ruin my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other types of delusions, such as delusions of grandeur, being controlled, or having a special mission, beyond the belief that these specific people are working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. It is solely the belief that they are coordinating behind my back to freeze me out of my practice and social circle. I am just convinced that there is an external plot to damage my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you believe these people's actions against you are specifically aimed at you, or if you think it's part of a larger plot that just happens to involve you?\n\nPatient: I am certain that this is specifically and personally aimed at me. Most days I just sit in my apartment with the TV on mute, ignoring everyone and feeling like I'm just going through the motions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, especially in relation to these beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't actually there. For me, it has really just been this constant, overwhelming feeling that these specific people are actively working together to ruin me. That is the only thing I've been experiencing, but it feels completely real.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where these thoughts of people working against you went away completely for at least a month, or have they been continuous since they started?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't gone away at all. The general feeling that people were against me started slowly two years ago and has gradually worsened, but over the last couple of months, the intense belief that they are actively coordinating to ruin me has been completely continuous without any breaks.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're in danger or that your life is being threatened by these people you believe are working against you?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've felt like my life was in direct physical danger, but I definitely haven't felt safe or welcome in certain spaces, which is why I've cut trips short and isolated myself. The constant anxiety and stress of feeling like they are coordinating to ruin me has just made it feel easier to stay hidden away. It's incredibly exhausting to carry that fear, even if it isn't a physical threat.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning, aside from what you've already mentioned, that you attribute to these beliefs or to any other reason?\n\nPatient: Yes, my professional practice has taken a massive hit—I've had to cut my hours way back and have lost several long-term clients because I just can't manage it anymore. Socially, I've become almost completely isolated, barely seeing my friends or family because I constantly cancel plans or avoid any events where I think those people might show up.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant disorganized thinking or speech, or exhibited any catatonic behavior, alongside these persistent beliefs about people working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't experienced any disorganized speech, confused thinking, or unusual physical behaviors like that. My main struggle is really just the constant worry about these people working together to ruin my reputation.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other types of delusions, such as delusions of grandeur, being controlled, or having a special mission, beyond the belief that these specific people are working against you?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. It is solely the belief that they are coordinating behind my back to freeze me out of my practice and social circle. My struggles have really just been centered around the constant stress regarding those people in my professional and art circles.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific actions or events that you believe will happen if these people succeed in their alleged plot against you, and how that affects your daily life and decisions?\n\nPatient: If they succeed, I believe they will completely freeze me out, ruin my reputation, and destroy my financial advisory practice.
